items.headline: Lead: The board still hasn't flipped — Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: I checked the app this morning and the board is still the November 2 board. Same snapshot, Week 8 games, twelve days old. It still lists Sam Darnold as Seattle's starter and knows nothing about Sunday.

Sunday still starts in Munich. Patriots at Lions kicks off at 9:30 a.m. ET, and inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff, so about 8:00 a.m. ET for that one. The overnight news that matters most: Rams star Puka Nacua is headed to injured reserve with a neck injury.

Nothing on the board applies to Sunday. Your number goes through Check — type in your book's line and price and the app runs it back through the model and gives you a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.
items.takeaway: The board is still the November 2 board, so nothing on it applies to Sunday — run your number through Check, and watch inactives about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Injuries: final designations are in — the names that decide Sunday
paragraphs: Out for Sunday: Vikings quarterback Kyler Murray and tight end T.J. Hockenson, Texans receiver Marvin Harrison Jr., 49ers receiver Mike Evans, Packers edge rusher Micah Parsons and running back Josh Jacobs. The Rams put Puka Nacua on injured reserve with a neck injury, and the Cardinals lost Michael Wilson for the year with a neck injury. Bills tackle Spencer Brown is doubtful with an ankle injury.

Questionable, and the list that matters: A.J. Brown and Rhamondre Stevenson in Munich, Amon-Ra St. Brown in Munich too — he is expected to play through his rib injury — Kenneth Walker in Atlanta, Trent Williams and Dre Greenlaw in Dallas, Garrett Wilson against Buffalo, Travis Etienne after a full practice Friday, and Denzel Boston, who is trending in the right direction.
Seattle is settled: Drew Lock starts again with no designation, Darnold, Cross, Nelson and Williams are out, and Nwosu, Shaheed and Pili are back with no designation.
items.takeaway: The questionable list that matters: A.J. Brown, Stevenson and Amon-Ra St. Brown in Munich, Kenneth Walker in Atlanta, Trent Williams in Dallas — inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff.

items.headline: Weather: nothing flagged, two games worth a glance
paragraphs: No wind flag anywhere on Sunday. Cleveland has the only rain chance and MetLife has the strongest gusts, and neither reaches the line that usually matters.
Weather is a fact to know, not a reason to bet a total. If the wind or rain changes before kickoff, the number you care about is still the one your book is offering — run it through Check.
items.takeaway: No wind flag anywhere on Sunday — Cleveland has the only rain chance and MetLife the strongest gusts, and neither reaches the line that usually matters.

items.headline: Sunday: thirteen games, starting in Munich at 9:30 a.m. ET

The Jaguars are the biggest favorite on the board at -10.5. 49ers at Cowboys carries the week's highest total at 55.5. The Lions are -2.5 against the Patriots.

sections.title: What It Means for NFL EDGE

items.headline: The board still has not flipped — Sunday still goes through Check
paragraphs: The board refreshes every morning and evening, but it is still showing the November 2 snapshot. It is twelve days old, it is still showing Week 8, and it still lists Darnold as Seattle's starter.

That does not leave you without the app. Tap Check, type in your book's line and price, and the app runs it back through the model and the evaluator and returns a bet or no-bet verdict on your price. It is a full re-evaluation, not a blind override.
If your book's number is different from the one on the board — and right now every book's number is different, because the board is twelve days old — Check is how you use the app today.
items.takeaway: The board is twelve days old and still showing Week 8, so Sunday's prices go through Check — type in your book's line and the app gives a bet or no-bet verdict on your price.

items.headline: The three cards, in plain English
paragraphs: Hit Rate is the supported pick that looks most likely to win. It gives up value to get the win. The app's own tutorial says it plainly: Hit Rate is not Profit Rate.
Balanced is a strong pick without paying too much. It is the middle ground, and a good starting point if you are new to this.

Value is always the model's plus-EV play. The number says the price is better than the true chance. Hit Rate and Balanced are not worse for not being plus-EV. They are different jobs. Pick the card that matches the job you want done.
items.takeaway: Hit Rate chases the win, Balanced chases a strong pick at a fair price, Value chases plus-EV — three different jobs, and none of them is the wrong card.

items.headline: Learn the Game: the vig — the price of placing the bet
paragraphs: The vig, also called the juice, is the book's cut. It is built into the price. At -110, every $1.10 you risk wins $1. The extra ten cents is the book's margin.

Hypothetical example, clearly labeled as hypothetical: a coin flip is a true 50-50. If a book offered both sides at -110, you would need to win about 52.4% of the time just to break even, because you pay $1.10 to win $1. That is the vig working against you.

That is why the app's Value card exists. It looks for prices where the model says the true chance beats the price even after the vig. And before you take any price, run it through Check and see what the app says about it.
items.takeaway: The vig is the book's cut — at -110 you risk $1.10 to win $1, so you need to win about 52.4% of the time just to break even.

items.headline: The big numbers have not moved since last night
paragraphs: The Jaguars are still -10.5, 49ers at Cowboys is still 55.5, and the Lions are still -2.5. Nothing in this morning's checks showed a move.

The board itself is unchanged too — still the November 2 snapshot, so there is no new app number to compare against. Any move that happens today will show up on your book first, and Check is how you test it.

On the splits: the free VSiN page this morning showed a college basketball row and no NFL row, so there is no fresh public-versus-money read. The last NFL split I could read, last night, had the Lions at -2.5 with the tickets and the money agreeing on the same side. That is not a Fade.
items.takeaway: Nothing moved since last night — Jaguars still -10.5, 49ers-Cowboys total still 55.5, Lions still -2.5, and the last split read had the public and the money agreeing, which is not a Fade.

items.headline: Today's job: know your questionable names before the Sunday rush
paragraphs: Saturday is prep. Know which questionable names your bets depend on: A.J. Brown, Stevenson and Amon-Ra St. Brown in the Munich game, Walker in Atlanta, Trent Williams in Dallas. Inactives land about 90 minutes before kickoff — about 8:00 a.m. ET for Munich.

Wait only for inactives if your bet needs a questionable player. Otherwise, if your book has a good number right now and Check says bet, bet it now. Waiting lets the number drift the wrong way too, and the Sunday late rush on big-name teams can push a line past the app's playable number.
One more thing, and it matters: settlement is manual. The tracker only works if you are honest with yourself. Log the losers too.
items.takeaway: Wait only for inactives if your bet needs a questionable player — otherwise, if your book has a good number and Check says bet, bet it now. And log the losers too: settlement is manual, and the tracker only works if you're honest with yourself.
